scenario.topic: Decide which programming language for a new internal tool
scenario.opening_question: What trade-offs are we willing to make between speed of development, maintainability, and integration?

options.name: Python with Django Framework
options.upside: Fast prototyping with extensive libraries and easy database integration
options.tradeoff: Moderate runtime performance may limit scalability under heavy load
options.concern: Some team members have limited Django experience which could slow initial progress

options.name: TypeScript with Node.js Backend
options.upside: Strong typing reduces bugs and runtime errors, with good performance
options.tradeoff: Longer initial setup and learning curve compared to scripting languages
options.concern: Requires careful architecture to avoid callback complexity and maintainability issues

options.name: Go with Gin Web Framework
options.upside: Excellent performance and concurrency support for scalable internal tools
options.tradeoff: Less mature ecosystem and fewer libraries compared to Python or Node.js
options.concern: Team has minimal Go experience, which could increase ramp-up time

options.name: Ruby on Rails Framework
options.upside: Very fast development with strong conventions and good database tooling
options.tradeoff: Runtime performance is moderate and may not scale well for complex tasks
options.concern: Some team members are unfamiliar with Ruby, which could slow initial progress

shared_context: The team consists of exactly 4 developers with varied experience
The internal tool must be delivered within 3 months
The tool will integrate with existing company databases and APIs
